---
title: "Replay a sample-alignment failure"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
description: >
  Record a failed named case, replay it from the same source and verify the fix.
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Replay a sample-alignment failure}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
---

A sample selection function should keep assay columns and sample metadata
in sync and return the samples in the requested order. This example uses a
deliberate bug in a small `SummarizedExperiment` to show how to record the
failure, replay it and check the fix. It uses the GitHub development build
of biocroxytest, SummarizedExperiment and testthat 3.3.0 or newer.

## Create a named regression case

Create a minimal source tree for the named-case runner. In an existing
package, add the roclet to its `Roxygen` field and put the case next to
the function it exercises.

```{r setup-package}
work <- tempfile("sample-alignment-")
pkg <- file.path(work, "samplealignment")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "tests", "testthat"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: samplealignment",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Imports: SummarizedExperiment",
  "Suggests: testthat (>= 3.3.0)",
  "Config/testthat/edition: 3",
  'Roxygen: list(roclets = "biocroxytest::tests_roclet")'
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
writeLines("export(align_samples)", file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
```

The case asks for `s3` followed by `s1`. The buggy implementation uses
membership to select columns, so it returns them in their original order.
The assertions specify the expected sample IDs, counts and conditions.

```{r write-case}
source_file <- file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R")
writeLines(r"(
#' @testCases sample-alignment
#' list(
#'   cases = list(reordered = list(suite = "tests")),
#'   test = {
#'     samples <- c("s1", "s2", "s3")
#'     counts <- matrix(c(11L, 21L, 31L), nrow = 1L,
#'                      dimnames = list("gene1", samples))
#'     metadata <- data.frame(condition = c("control", "control", "treated"),
#'                            row.names = samples)
#'     x <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
#'       assays = list(counts = counts), colData = metadata
#'     )
#'     aligned <- align_samples(x, c("s3", "s1"))
#'     expect_identical(colnames(aligned), c("s3", "s1"))
#'     expect_identical(as.integer(SummarizedExperiment::assay(aligned)),
#'                      c(31L, 11L))
#'     expect_identical(aligned$condition, c("treated", "control"))
#'   }
#' )
align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, colnames(x) %in% samples]
)", source_file)
```

## Run, record and replay

Generate the test and run it by its stable case ID. For this example,
`load_source` lets roxygen read the source without attaching the temporary
package. The runner returns the failure as evidence, so the document
build can verify the expected outcome.

```{r run-failure, message=FALSE}
invisible(roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg, load_code = roxygen2::load_source))
id <- "sample-alignment/reordered"
failed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id, seed = 42L)
stopifnot(identical(failed$cases$status, "failed"))
cat(failed$cases$detail, "\n", sep = "")
```

Save the record outside the source tree. Replay uses the same source
revision and the recorded seed. A matching result means the failure
signature was reproduced. Keep the matching source if you plan to replay
after editing the package.

```{r replay-failure}
record_file <- file.path(work, "alignment-failure.rds")
biocroxytest::write_test_replay(failed, id, record_file)
replayed <- biocroxytest::replay_test_case(record_file, path = pkg)
stopifnot(isTRUE(replayed$comparison$same_failure))
replayed$comparison$same_failure
```

## Verify the fix

Select columns by sample name in the requested order. Keep the same
assertions and require the case to complete without warnings, as you
would in CI.

```{r verify-fix}
code <- readLines(source_file)
code[startsWith(code, "align_samples <-")] <-
  "align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, samples]"
writeLines(code, source_file)

fixed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id, seed = 42L)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(fixed, required = id)
fixed$cases[c("id", "status")]
```

Commit the corrected function and its generated regression test in your
package. In this walkthrough, the source package and replay record are
temporary and can be removed together.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
